Senses.Explanation: The records coordinate confusion and awakening as a tested pair, repeatedly setting it beside ordinary and holy, motion and stillness, and true and false. Literally the graphs say "be lost or confused" (迷) and "awaken or understand" (悟): "confusion and awakening," attested 1,115 times in 231 allowlisted texts. The pair is repeatedly coordinated with ordinary and holy, motion and stillness, and true and false. One verse says, "the nature of confusion and awakening is empty; that empty nature has neither end nor beginning" (迷悟性皆空，性空無終始). Zhongxuan asks, "ordinary and holy are originally not two; how could confusion and awakening have different roads?" (凡聖本來不二，迷悟豈有殊途). Zhe'an says, "confusion and awakening are not different; motion and stillness have one source" (迷悟不異，動靜一源).
Senses.Note: The records also correct bare negation of the pair. A quoted line says, "originally there is no person of confusion or awakening; only understand today" (本無迷悟人，祇要今日了); the named record subject immediately asks, "if there is no confusion or awakening, what do you understand?" (既無迷悟，了箇甚麼). Zhe'an likewise says that claiming confusion and awakening no longer exist is still halfway, then asks for confusion not to obstruct awakening and awakening not to obstruct confusion. These are explicit textual relations, not separate senses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)); Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書), Zhongyan Huimu Yunneng section: Zhongyan replies, ‘If there is neither confusion nor awakening, what do you understand?’ The preceding Longji quotation is discussed in the prose but is not conflated with this exact turn.

The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhean Fan (蔗菴範禪師語錄), in Zhean Jingfan's own winter-solstice hall address. Zhean Jingfan is the exact speaker pairing confusion and awakening as not different and motion and stillness as one source. The source's Yunmen heading is a monastery/place association, not Yunmen Wenyan speaking.
